paras.en: Cerny graduated from Morton East High School in Cicero in 1966, then earned his bachelor’s degree in Speech & Drama from Valparaiso University — he had planned to enter the seminary — and his master’s in Theater from Northwestern University.
paras.zh: 塞尔尼 1966 年毕业于西塞罗的莫顿东高中，随后在瓦尔帕莱索大学获得演讲与戏剧学士学位（他原本计划进入神学院），并在西北大学获得戏剧硕士学位。

paras.en: In the 1970s, he joined The Second City to perform improv on its mainstage in Chicago and for its national touring company.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 70 年代，他加入了 The Second City，在芝加哥的主舞台及其全国巡回演出公司进行即兴表演。

paras.en: He played a desk clerk in Somewhere in Time (1980), a tailor in My Best Friend’s Wedding (1997) and a banker in Road to Perdition (2002).
paras.zh: 他在《某处时光》（1980）中扮演一名前台服务员，在《我最好朋友的婚礼》（1997）中扮演一名裁缝，在《毁灭之路》（2002）中扮演一名银行家。

paras.en: The gregarious Cerny also showed up on the big screen in Rent-a-Cop (1987), Mo’ Money (1992), Love and Action in Chicago (1999), Novocaine (2001) and Legally Blonde 2: Red, White & Blonde (2003) and on episodes of Lady Blue, Early Edition and Chicago Hope.
paras.zh: 爱交际的塞尔尼还出现在大银幕上的《租个警察》（1987年）、《金钱》（1992年）、《芝加哥的爱情与行动》（1999年）、《奴佛卡因》（2001年）和《律政俏佳人2：红白金发》（2003年）以及《蓝色女士》、《早期版》和《芝加哥希望》的剧集中。

paras.en: Cerny wrote a weekly column for Screen Magazine called “ADventures in Advertising,” drove go-karts well into his 60s and was an enthusiastic model train collector.
paras.zh: 塞尔尼为《Screen》杂志撰写了每周专栏，名为“广告冒险”，他在 60 多岁时还开着卡丁车，还是一位热情的火车模型收藏家。

paras.en: Survivors include his wife of 56 years, Eileen; sons Tim and Patrick; daughters-in-law Andrea and Lily; and grandchildren Archer and Cleo.
paras.zh: 幸存者包括与他结婚 56 年的妻子艾琳 (Eileen)；儿子蒂姆和帕特里克；儿媳妇安德里亚和莉莉；以及孙子阿切尔和克莱奥。

paras.en: “I’m lucky, I get to be somebody different every day, and in the end, I’m glad I stuck with my irresponsible decision to have fun,” he once said. “It allows me to live happily ever after … every day.”
paras.zh: “我很幸运，我每天都能成为不同的人，最后，我很高兴我坚持了我不负责任的决定来享受乐趣，”他曾经说过。 “它让我从此过上幸福的生活......每一天。”

articles.title: Traders bet on a pop for Anthropic's historic IPO

paras.en: News of Anthropic's historic initial public offering provided a wave of relief for tech investors. The response in the perpetual futures market might provide even more relief.
paras.zh: Anthropic 历史性首次公开募股的消息让科技投资者松了一口气。永续期货市场的反应可能会带来更多的缓解。

paras.en: As Anthropic prepares to raise money in its initial public offering this month, traders in offshore markets are making large bets that there will be a big pop on the AI giant's debut.
paras.zh: 随着 Anthropic 准备在本月的首次公开募股中筹集资金，离岸市场的交易员纷纷押注这家人工智能巨头的首次亮相将会大受欢迎。

paras.en: Trying to guess an initial first day IPO reaction is nearly impossible, but a new and fast-growing corner of the markets might offer some clues.
paras.zh: 试图猜测 IPO 首日的最初反应几乎是不可能的，但市场中一个快速增长的新角落可能会提供一些线索。

paras.en: Pre-IPO perpetuals, contracts that aim to track the price of private companies, trade on decentralized crypto exchanges like Hyperliquid, Coinbase, Binance and OKX to name a few. The current Hyperliquid Anthropic contract implies a stock price of $98 and its market cap at roughly $1.7 trillion, more than 30% higher than the $70-$78 range announced in the company's updated S1.
paras.zh: Pre-IPO 永续合约是旨在跟踪私营公司价格的合约，在 Hyperliquid、Coinbase、Binance 和 OKX 等去中心化加密货币交易所进行交易。当前的 Hyperliquid Anthropic 合约意味着股价为 98 美元，市值约为 1.7 万亿美元，比该公司更新的 S1 中宣布的 70-78 美元区间高出 30% 以上。

paras.en: While trading on the exchange is not currently available to American investors, about $250 million of volume traded across Hyperliquid's two Anthropic trackers in the past 24 hours, according to the exchange.
paras.zh: 据该交易所称，虽然美国投资者目前无法在该交易所进行交易，但过去 24 小时内 Hyperliquid 的两个 Anthropic 追踪器的交易量约为 2.5 亿美元。

paras.en: Hyperliquid's pre-IPO Anthropic perp began trading two weeks ago at $138 before settling into a roughly ten-dollar range between $110 and $120 prior to last week's selloff in tech stocks, as the contract slipped below $94 at one point.
paras.zh: Hyperliquid 的首次公开募股前 Anthropic 永续合约两周前开始交易，价格为 138 美元，随后在上周科技股抛售之前，该合约一度跌破 94 美元，价格区间在 110 美元至 120 美元之间，大约 10 美元。

paras.en: To proponents of this new asset class, the pricing of the perps is evidence that bankers intentionally undersell equity ahead of IPOs to ensure a post-market "pop." Looking at SpaceX, the argument rings true: pre-IPO perps on SpaceX traded at a premium and converged with equity prices at the IPO, all before shares went on a three-day rally of as much as 40% in the immediate aftermath of the listing.
paras.zh: 对于这一新资产类别的支持者来说，永续债券的定价证明银行家在首次公开募股之前故意抛售股票，以确保上市后的“流行”。看看 SpaceX，这个论点是正确的：SpaceX 的 IPO 前股票交易价格溢价，并与 IPO 时的股价趋同，而所有这些都是在上市后股价连续三天上涨 40% 之多之前。

paras.en: News of Anthropic's upcoming roadshow may be weighing on competitor OpenAI. Perps tracking OpenAI's market cap dropped 7% to $1.27 trillion, according to Hyperliquid trading on a contract trading $2.8 billion in volume over the past 24 hours.
paras.zh: Anthropic 即将举行路演的消息可能会给竞争对手 OpenAI 带来压力。根据 Hyperliquid 的数据，追踪 OpenAI 市值的 Perps 下跌 7%，至 1.27 万亿美元，过去 24 小时合约交易量达 28 亿美元。

paras.en: Shares of Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR), the publicly-traded Treasury company investing in the HYPE tokens that power the exchange fell 4% Tuesday. The stock is up 150% on the year.
paras.zh: Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR) 是一家上市财务公司，投资于为交易所提供动力的 HYPE 代币，周二股价下跌 4%。该股今年以来上涨了150%。

articles.title: Jim Jordan elected House GOP leader

paras.en: House Republicans picked Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio to serve as minority leader in the next Congress, news outlets reported Tuesday after a closed-door vote.
paras.zh: 据新闻媒体周二在闭门投票后报道，众议院共和党人选择俄亥俄州众议员吉姆乔丹担任下一届国会的少数党领袖。

paras.en: Jordan, the House Judiciary Committee chairman, was elected in a 106-73 vote, sources told MS NOW on condition of anonymity to discuss the private meeting.
paras.zh: 消息人士在不愿透露姓名的情况下向 MS NOW 透露，讨论这次非公开会议时，众议院司法委员会主席乔丹以 106 比 73 当选。

paras.en: A two-decade House veteran and committed supporter of President Donald Trump, Jordan will take on the leadership role just as Republicans relinquish power, following blowout Democratic victories in last week's midterm election.
paras.zh: 乔丹是众议院二十年的资深人士，也是唐纳德·特朗普总统的坚定支持者，在民主党在上周中期选举中取得井喷式胜利后，共和党将放弃权力，乔丹将担任领导角色。

paras.en: House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., announced the day after Election Day that he would not run for minority leader in the 120th Congress.
paras.zh: 众议院议长、路易斯安那州共和党人迈克·约翰逊 (Mike Johnson) 在选举日后的第二天宣布，他不会竞选第 120 届国会的少数党领袖。

paras.en: "I couldn't be more thrilled to see @Jim_Jordan elected House GOP leader," Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, wrote on X after Tuesday's vote.
paras.zh: “看到 @Jim_Jordan 当选众议院共和党领袖，我感到无比兴奋，”德克萨斯州共和党众议员布兰登·吉尔 (Brandon Gill) 在周二投票后在 X 上写道。

paras.en: "He's the original congressional brawler and is exactly what our Conference needs to lead us back to the majority," Gill wrote.
paras.zh: 吉尔写道：“他是最初的国会斗殴者，正是我们会议所需要的人来带领我们重新获得多数席位。”

articles.title: Nvidia hires law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead Jensen Huang affair probe

paras.en: Nvidia's board of directors said on Tuesday that it hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang and whether company secrets or national security was compromised, after Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman who has been connected to Chinese intelligence.
paras.zh: 英伟达董事会周二表示，在黄仁勋承认与一名与中国情报部门有联系的女性有染后，它聘请了 Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz 对首席执行官黄仁勋进行调查，调查公司机密或国家安全是否受到损害。

paras.en: "The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday," the board said in a statement.
paras.zh: “NVIDIA 董事会的独立成员已聘请纽约南区前代理美国检察官 Joon H. Kim 及其公司 Wachtell、Lipton、Rosen & Katz 进行彻底、独立的调查，正如周日宣布的那样，”董事会在一份声明中表示。

paras.en: Kim joined the firm last month, and he was previously the chief U.S. prosecutor in Manhattan, according to Law360.
paras.zh: 据 Law360 报道，金上个月加入该公司，此前他曾担任曼哈顿的美国首席检察官。

paras.en: Nvidia has been thrust into turmoil since Huang's acknowledgement of the affair over the weekend. The chipmaker's stock dropped 6% on Tuesday after falling more than 4% on Monday, as investors worry that the investigation and scandal could result in the co-founder and CEO being forced out.
paras.zh: 自从黄在周末承认此事以来，英伟达陷入了混乱。该芯片制造商的股价在周一下跌超过 4% 后，周二下跌 6%，原因是投资者担心调查和丑闻可能导致联合创始人兼首席执行官被迫离职。

paras.en: Nvidia and the board are facing pressure from critics and politicians over what the company knew about sales of its restricted AI chips to Chinese companies.
paras.zh: 英伟达和董事会正面临来自批评者和政界人士的压力，因为该公司对向中国公司销售其受限制的人工智能芯片的情况知情。

paras.en: Over the past few weeks, The New York Times and Financial Times have reported that U.S. intelligence agencies surveilled an Asian technology executive, Alice Huang, who has been affiliated with Nvidia customer Megaspeed. These agencies have concluded that she is passing information to Beijing and is involved with Chinese intelligence, according to the reports.
paras.zh: 过去几周，《纽约时报》和《金融时报》报道称，美国情报机构监视了一位与 Nvidia 客户 Megaspeed 有关联的亚洲科技高管 Alice Huang。据报道，这些机构得出的结论是，她正在向北京传递信息并参与中国情报工作。

paras.en: Huang has become the face of the AI industry, going by his first name "Jensen" to customers and rivals as Nvidia's technology is used to train nearly all major AI models. The chipmaker has become an essential source of financing for AI startups and Huang has met with presidents and CEOs around the world as Nvidia's public face.
paras.zh: 黄仁勋已经成为人工智能行业的代言人，他的名字是“Jensen”，客户和竞争对手都称呼他为“Jensen”，因为英伟达的技术被用来训练几乎所有主要的人工智能模型。这家芯片制造商已成为人工智能初创公司的重要融资来源，黄仁勋作为 Nvidia 的公众形象会见了世界各地的总裁和首席执行官。

paras.en: But Huang's actions have thrown the chipmaker into instability as he admitted to an affair with Alice Huang in an email to staff on Sunday.
paras.zh: 但黄的行为让这家芯片制造商陷入了不稳定，因为他在周日发给员工的电子邮件中承认与爱丽丝黄有染。

paras.en: "My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," Huang wrote in the message, while emphasizing that he is an American and supports U.S. national security.
paras.zh: 黄在邮件中写道：“我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。”他同时强调自己是美国人，支持美国国家安全。

paras.en: An Nvidia representative said at the time that Huang was committed to continuing as CEO of Nvidia without interruption.
paras.zh: 英伟达代表当时表示，黄仁勋承诺不间断地继续担任英伟达首席执行官。

paras.en: On Sunday, Nvidia's board said that it would investigate the allegations that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
paras.zh: 周日，英伟达董事会表示，将调查有关黄仁勋成为外国情报工作目标的指控。

paras.en: Nvidia's board also said on Sunday that it has no reason to believe either national security nor Nvidia secrets were compromised.
paras.zh: 英伟达董事会周日还表示，没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达机密遭到泄露。

paras.en: This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.
paras.zh: 这是突发新闻。请刷新以获取更新。

articles.title: Virtual fruit fly brains can play Doom and trade bitcoin

paras.en: When scientists revealed the first in-depth map of a male fruit fly’s brain and nervous system—its connectome—in early September, neuroscience researchers rejoiced. Fruit flies are a key animal model, and studying their brains can help illuminate pathways and functions our species share.
paras.zh: 九月初，当科学家们首次揭示了雄性果蝇大脑和神经系统（连接组）的深度图谱时，神经科学研究人员欣喜若狂。果蝇是一种重要的动物模型，研究它们的大脑可以帮助阐明我们物种共有的途径和功能。

paras.en: Then the chronically online got hold of it. With access to the public dataset for the atlas, people soon set the “fly” to work in various virtual environments—from the video game Doom to bitcoin trading sites.
paras.zh: 然后长期上网的人就掌握了它。通过访问地图集的公共数据集，人们很快就将“飞行”设置为在各种虚拟环境中工作——从视频游戏《毁灭战士》到比特币交易网站。

paras.en: “It’s certainly an unexpected application of producing a connectome, but it’s fun, and it puts a spotlight on the research and allows the general public to get an entry into an otherwise complicated and difficult topic,” says Gerald M. Rubin, head of biology at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute Janelia Research Campus in Virginia and one of the researchers behind the dataset.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚州霍华德休斯医学研究所珍利亚研究园的生物学负责人、该数据集背后的研究人员之一杰拉尔德·M·鲁宾 (Gerald M. Rubin) 表示：“生成连接组确实是一种意想不到的应用，但它很有趣，它让研究成为人们关注的焦点，并让公众能够了解一个原本复杂而困难的话题。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: This connectome, which includes more than 166,000 neurons’ shapes and sizes, as well as the connections among them, is the fourth extensive map of its kind in flies and builds on two decades of study aimed at understanding how brains work. Researchers say this dataset, the first from a male fruit fly, is particularly intriguing for analyzing brain similarities and differences between sexes.
paras.zh: 这个连接组包含超过 166,000 个神经元的形状和大小，以及它们之间的连接，是果蝇中第四个广泛的此类图谱，建立在二十年旨在了解大脑如何工作的研究基础上。研究人员表示，这个数据集是第一个来自雄性果蝇的数据集，对于分析性别之间大脑的相似性和差异特别有趣。

paras.en: But researchers are quick to caveat: this is not an “uploaded” brain.
paras.zh: 但研究人员很快警告说：这不是一个“上传”的大脑。

paras.en: Bing Wen Brunton, a computational neuroscientist at the University of Washington in Seattle, says many programmers uploaded the connectome dataset to an artificial-intelligence model, which could then take the catalog and train it to do a task—such as playing chess or video games.
paras.zh: 西雅图华盛顿大学的计算神经科学家 Bing Wen Brunton 表示，许多程序员将连接组数据集上传到人工智能模型，然后该模型可以获取目录并训练它执行任务，例如下棋或视频游戏。

paras.en: Neurons are essentially processing machines: they receive inputs, then use different parameters to determine how to respond, often by releasing a signal to connected neurons. The model parameters change every time the virtual “fly” gets closer to accomplishing its task—in other words, the connectome shifts, Brunton says. “It’s being modified, sometimes by a lot, until it accomplishes the task the programmer has set out for it to do,” she explains.
paras.zh: 神经元本质上是处理机器：它们接收输入，然后使用不同的参数来确定如何响应，通常是向连接的神经元释放信号。 The model parameters change every time the virtual “fly” gets closer to accomplishing its task—in other words, the connectome shifts, Brunton says. “它会被修改，有时会被修改很多，直到它完成程序员设定的任务，”她解释道。

paras.en: Brunton studies how neural activity relates to the physical body, and she says we’re far from a sci-fi-like “brain upload” to a virtual environment or a machine. But as long as people don’t think flies are actually playing video games, she adds, “if the broader public is really engaging with this dataset and having fun with it, what else do we want as scientists?”
paras.zh: 布伦顿研究神经活动与身体的关系，她说我们距离科幻小说中的“大脑上传”到虚拟环境或机器还很远。但她补充道，只要人们不认为苍蝇实际上是在玩电子游戏，“如果更广泛的公众真正参与这个数据集并从中获得乐趣，那么作为科学家，我们还想要什么呢？”

paras.en: Connectome datasets have been publicly available before, but this release coincided with the rise of AI “vibe coding,” and its popularity only grew with the “memeability” of flies doing absurd things, says Nick Walton, founder and CEO of AI game company Latitude. Walton has played around with the dataset himself, training it, for instance, to solve a Rubik’s Cube.
paras.zh: 人工智能游戏公司 Latitude 的创始人兼首席执行官尼克·沃尔顿 (Nick Walton) 表示，Connectome 数据集之前就已公开，但这次发布恰逢人工智能“vibe 编码”的兴起，而且它的受欢迎程度只会随着苍蝇做荒谬事情的“可记忆性”而增长。沃尔顿自己也研究过这个数据集，例如训练它来解决魔方问题。

paras.en: Walton knows there isn’t a fly’s mind in his computer, but the intersection of biological intelligence and AI still intrigues him. “Is this way more advanced than just training something with a machine-learning model? Not really,” he says. “It’s more a capture of this underlying idea of what happens if you upload beings with biological intelligence into a digital world.”
paras.zh: 沃尔顿知道他的计算机中没有苍蝇的思维，但生物智能和人工智能的交叉仍然引起他的兴趣。 “这种方式比仅仅使用机器学习模型进行训练更先进吗？并非如此，”他说。 “它更多地捕捉到了如果将具有生物智能的生物上传到数字世界会发生什么的基本想法。”

articles.title: Oil prices are so high that CO2 emissions from fossil fuels are dropping

paras.en: The U.S. war with Iran has raised fossil fuel prices so much that the resulting drop in oil demand has put the world on track to see a rare dip in carbon emissions from these sources in 2026.
paras.zh: 美国与伊朗的战争导致化石燃料价格大幅上涨，导致石油需求下降，全球这些来源的碳排放量有望在 2026 年出现罕见下降。

paras.en: Between 2019 and 2025, carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels grew by about 0.8 percent annually, according to a new study published in Nature Climate Change. But 2026 is set to buck that trend: high oil prices, as well as the continued rise of green technology—solar power, wind and electric cars—will cause a “short-term” 0.4 percent drop, according to the study.
paras.zh: 根据《自然气候变化》发表的一项新研究，2019 年至 2025 年间，化石燃料产生的二氧化碳排放量每年增长约 0.8%。但研究表明，2026 年将扭转这一趋势：高油价以及太阳能、风能和电动汽车等绿色技术的持续崛起将导致“短期”下降 0.4%。

paras.en: “The high petrol prices following the war in Iran are reducing oil use and keeping emissions low,” says the study’s lead author Corinne Le Quéré, a professor of climate change science at the University of East Anglia in England. “But that’s not the whole story: The expansion of renewable energy has progressed a lot in recent years, led by China. And [along with electric vehicles], this is offsetting two thirds of the growing demand for energy.”
paras.zh: 该研究的主要作者、英国东安格利亚大学气候变化科学教授 Corinne Le Quéré 表示：“伊朗战争后的高油价正在减少石油使用并保持低排放。” “但这还不是故事的全部：近年来，在中国的引领下，可再生能源的扩张取得了很大进展。[连同电动汽车]，这抵消了能源需求增长的三分之二。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: With all sources of carbon considered, including deforestation, total global CO2 emissions are set to continue increasing.
paras.zh: 考虑到所有碳源，包括森林砍伐，全球二氧化碳排放总量将继续增加。

paras.en: The findings come as the United Nations’ climate talks get underway in Antalya, Türkiye, and during a year marred by global temperature extremes and climate disasters. This year is on track to be among the hottest on record.
paras.zh: 这一发现是在联合国气候谈判在土耳其安塔利亚举行之际发布的，而这一年正值全球极端气温和气候灾难的影响。今年有望成为有记录以来最热的一年之一。

paras.en: The drop in emissions is also notable because it is the first annual reduction since the COVID pandemic, when emissions dropped by an estimated 5 percent or so, Le Quéré says. Researchers also measured a small decrease in emissions after the 2008 recession. “However, in both cases, emissions rebounded the year after,” Le Quéré says.
paras.zh: Le Quéré 表示，排放量的下降也很引人注目，因为这是自新冠疫情大流行以来排放量首次下降，当时排放量估计下降了 5% 左右。研究人员还测量到 2008 年经济衰退后排放量略有下降。 “然而，在这两种情况下，排放量在第二年都出现反弹，”勒奎雷说。

paras.en: If oil prices return to their prewar levels, Le Quéré and her colleagues expect to see emissions rise once more. But the “rebound” could be countered by further adding renewable energy to the world’s portfolio, she adds.
paras.zh: 如果油价恢复到战前水平，勒奎雷和她的同事预计排放量将再次上升。但她补充道，“反弹”可能会通过在全球能源组合中进一步增加可再生能源来抵消。

paras.en: “We show that to tackle climate change and guarantee that global fossil emissions decrease durably, the expansion of renewable energy and electric vehicles need to accelerate further,” Le Quéré says.
paras.zh: “我们表明，为了应对气候变化并确保全球化石排放量持续减少，可再生能源和电动汽车的扩张需要进一步加速，”勒奎雷说。

articles.title: The U.S. may be on the cusp of losing its measles elimination status

paras.en: The U.S. is almost certainly no longer deserving of its measles elimination status, public health experts say—and the nation could officially lose it as soon as this week. Officials at the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) are meeting to discuss whether the country has seen enough endemic spread of the potentially deadly and highly preventable disease to warrant taking away that accolade. If PAHO does opt to remove the elimination status, the loss will represent a public health failure of the highest degree, experts say.
paras.zh: 公共卫生专家表示，美国几乎肯定不再值得获得消除麻疹的地位，而且该国最早可能在本周正式失去这一地位。泛美卫生组织（PAHO）的官员正在开会讨论该国是否已经看到这种潜在致命且高度可预防的疾病的流行程度足以导致剥夺这一荣誉。专家表示，如果泛美卫生组织确实选择取消消除状态，这种损失将代表最高程度的公共卫生失败。

paras.en: “It’s astounding to me,” says Elizabeth Jacobs, a professor emeritus at the University of Arizona. “I’m just beside myself about all of this. I literally cannot believe this is happening in the United States.”
paras.zh: “这让我感到震惊，”亚利桑那大学名誉教授伊丽莎白·雅各布斯说。 “我对这一切感到非常震惊。我简直不敢相信这种事发生在美国。”

paras.en: The sixth annual meeting of PAHO’s Measles and Rubella Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission runs from November 10 to 13. At the meeting, an international team of experts in epidemiology, public health, virology and other medical fields assess the status of these diseases in the Americas. The U.S. was declared to have eliminated measles in 2000—what this means is that the disease did not spread within the country for an entire year. Isolated cases remained possible but would be quickly contained.
paras.zh: 泛美卫生组织消除麻疹和风疹区域监测和再验证委员会第六次年会于11月10日至13日举行。会上，流行病学、公共卫生、病毒学和其他医学领域的国际专家小组评估了美洲这些疾病的状况。美国于2000年宣布消灭麻疹，这意味着该疾病整整一年都没有在该国境内传播。个别病例仍有可能出现，但很快就会得到遏制。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: For the past two years, successive measles outbreaks around the country have expanded at rates that haven’t been seen in decades. So far in 2026, there have been 5,182 confirmed cases of measles, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. That’s up from 2,289 in all of 2025 and just 285 in 2024. The disease has been detected in almost every state, and local health departments have reported eight deaths connected to the outbreaks this year. (The CDC has recorded four deaths.)
paras.zh: 过去两年来，全国各地连续爆发麻疹疫情，其蔓延速度是几十年来从未有过的。据美国疾病控制与预防中心称，截至 2026 年，已有 5,182 例麻疹确诊病例。这一数字高于 2025 年全年的 2,289 例和 2024 年的 285 例。几乎每个州都发现了这种疾病，当地卫生部门报告今年有 8 人因疫情爆发死亡。 （疾病预防控制中心记录了四人死亡。）

paras.en: Revoking the U.S.’s elimination status would merely recognize what’s been a fact on the ground for months, says Michael Osterholm, director of the Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy at the University of Minnesota.
paras.zh: 明尼苏达大学传染病研究与政策中心主任迈克尔·奥斯特霍尔姆表示，取消美国的消除状态只会承认几个月来的事实。

paras.en: “When a semi hits your car at 60 miles an hour at an intersection, you don’t need more assessments showing you’ve had an accident,” he says.
paras.zh: “当一辆半挂车在十字路口以每小时 60 英里的速度撞上你的车时，你不需要更多的评估来证明你发生了事故，”他说。

paras.en: Revoking the U.S.’s elimination status would hold no formal consequences but would be a blow to the wealthiest country in the world and its public health system. Many public health experts blame the Department of Health and Human Services, which Jacobs describes as an “epidemiological crime scene” under the leadership of Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.
paras.zh: 取消美国的淘汰地位不会产生正式后果，但会对世界上最富有的国家及其公共卫生系统造成打击。许多公共卫生专家指责卫生与公众服务部，雅各布斯将其描述为小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪领导下的“流行病犯罪现场”。

paras.en: Kennedy, a longtime vaccine critic, has occasionally recommended that parents get their kids the mumps, measles and rubella (MMR) vaccine, but he has also recommended ineffective treatments for the disease and sowed doubt as to the effectiveness and safety of vaccines for years.
paras.zh: 肯尼迪是一位长期的疫苗批评者，他偶尔会建议父母给孩子接种腮腺炎、麻疹和风疹 (MMR) 疫苗，但他也建议对该疾病采取无效的治疗方法，多年来对疫苗的有效性和安全性产生了怀疑。

paras.en: “I’ve seen Kennedy say that the reason that this is happening is because parents didn’t get their kids vaccinated during COVID. And to the extent that that is true, he has been in office for 18 months,” Jacobs says. “He has had ample time to go and form a really rigorous and thorough vaccination program, and he can barely say that MMR vaccination is the only way to prevent measles effectively.” HHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
paras.zh: “我看到肯尼迪说，发生这种情况的原因是父母在新冠病毒期间没有让孩子接种疫苗。如果确实如此，他已经上任 18 个月了，”雅各布斯说。 “他有足够的时间去制定一个非常严格和彻底的疫苗接种计划，他几乎不能说 MMR 疫苗接种是有效预防麻疹的唯一方法。”美国卫生与公众服务部没有立即回应置评请求。

paras.en: Around the country, vaccination rates have been in decline for years. The percentage of children who received the MMR vaccine has fallen below the 95 percent rate that is required to sustain herd immunity. According to the CDC, 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated against measles in 2026, down from 95.2 percent in 2020. Rates vary by state; 18 states have MMR vaccination rates below 90 percent, with Idaho, for example, reporting a rate of just 75.2 percent.
paras.zh: 在全国各地，疫苗接种率多年来一直在下降。接受 MMR 疫苗的儿童比例已降至维持群体免疫所需的 95% 以下。根据 CDC 的数据，到 2026 年，92.4% 的幼儿园儿童接种了麻疹疫苗，低于 2020 年的 95.2%。各个州的接种率有所不同；有 18 个州的 MMR 疫苗接种率低于 90%，例如爱达荷州的疫苗接种率仅为 75.2%。

paras.en: Those numbers don't reflect the true extent of the crisis, Osterholm says. Vaccination rates can vary wildly within states, leading to pockets of people who are unprotected against measles. A study in Nature Health in January, for example, found numerous counties across the country with MMR vaccination coverage under 60 percent.
paras.zh: 奥斯特霍尔姆说，这些数字并不能反映危机的真实程度。各州之间的疫苗接种率差异很大，导致少数人无法预防麻疹。例如，《自然健康》杂志 1 月份的一项研究发现，全国许多县的 MMR 疫苗接种覆盖率低于 60%。

paras.en: “There's an old line that describes this well: When your head’s in the freezer and your feet are in the oven, you’re, on average, very comfortable,” Osterholm says. “We have a situation right now where, in a state like Minnesota, with one of the most progressive public health departments in the country, we have schools that have 80 percent level of vaccination, [and] we have a number of school districts that are at the 40 percent level.”
paras.zh: “有一句老话很好地描述了这一点：当你的头在冰箱里、脚在烤箱里时，平均而言，你会感到非常舒服，”奥斯特霍尔姆说。 “我们现在的情况是，在像明尼苏达州这样拥有全国最进步的公共卫生部门之一的州，我们的学校的疫苗接种率达到了 80%，[而且]我们有许多学区的疫苗接种率达到了 40%。”

paras.en: More than 40 percent of the U.S. measles cases this year have occurred in people aged 20 or older. Given that 96 percent of all measles cases were in people who were either unvaccinated or whose vaccinations status was unknown, many of these adults likely didn’t get vaccinated as children.
paras.zh: 今年美国 40% 以上的麻疹病例发生在 20 岁或以上的人群中。鉴于 96% 的麻疹病例都是未接种疫苗或疫苗接种状况未知的人，因此这些成年人中的许多人可能在儿童时期没有接种疫苗。

paras.en: Jacobs says that while antivaccine sentiment has been brewing for years, the rise of social media has “supercharged” the problem. “This whole thing blew up right around the same time Facebook did, and I could see it happening, and there's no way to stop it,” she says.
paras.zh: 雅各布斯表示，尽管反疫苗情绪已经酝酿多年，但社交媒体的兴起“加剧”了这个问题。 “这整件事大约在 Facebook 发生的同时爆发，我可以看到它的发生，但没有办法阻止它，”她说。

paras.en: Osterholm warns that the situation could get much worse, pointing to Canada as an example. Last year PAHO revoked Canada’s measles elimination status after the country recorded more than 5,000 cases.
paras.zh: 奥斯特霍尔姆警告说，情况可能会变得更糟，并以加拿大为例。去年，在加拿大记录了超过 5,000 例麻疹病例后，泛美卫生组织取消了加拿大的麻疹消除地位。

paras.en: “That was in a population of 40 million,” he says. “Here we are sitting at 350 million, and if we were to see similar rates as Canada saw, that would be over 50,000 cases of measles a year.”
paras.zh: “那是在 4000 万人口中，”他说。 “我们现在有 3.5 亿人，如果我们看到与加拿大类似的比率，那么每年麻疹病例将超过 5 万例。”

paras.en: Canada can also offer some hope. Jacobs points out that last month Canada’s outbreak was declared over.
paras.zh: 加拿大也可以带来一些希望。雅各布斯指出，上个月加拿大的疫情已被宣布结束。

paras.en: For the U.S. to follow suit, urgent action would be needed on the part of state and federal health authorities. If that doesn’t happen, Jacobs warns that there could be more infectious disease outbreaks on the horizon.
paras.zh: 为了让美国效仿，州和联邦卫生当局需要采取紧急行动。雅各布斯警告说，如果这种情况没有发生，可能会出现更多传染病的爆发。

paras.en: “As vaccination rates decrease, measles pops up first because it’s so contagious,” she says. “But the other vaccine-preventable diseases are simmering in the background, and as we have learned, it really doesn’t take much for things to start tearing through a population.”
paras.zh: “随着疫苗接种率下降，麻疹首先出现，因为它的传染性很强，”她说。 “但其他疫苗可预防的疾病正在幕后酝酿，据我们所知，实际上并不需要太多的时间，事情就开始在人群中蔓延。”

articles.title: This may be the best evidence yet that dinosaur blood can fossilize
articles.author: Carolyn Gramling

paras.en: The life and times of a dinosaur may be written in its blood — if blood can be preserved in bone.
paras.zh: 恐龙的一生和时代可能会写在它的血液中——如果血液可以保存在骨头里的话。

paras.en: Tiny microstructures found in the limb bones of a fossilized 115-million-year-old specimen are the remnants of red blood cells, researchers report November 2 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The team says these are both the oldest red blood cell structures yet identified and the first to be chemically proven. But not everyone is as sanguine about that conclusion.
paras.zh: 研究人员 11 月 2 日在《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，在 1.15 亿年前的化石标本的四肢骨中发现的微小微观结构是红细胞的残留物。研究小组表示，这些都是迄今为止发现的最古老的红细胞结构，也是第一个得到化学证明的红细胞结构。但并非所有人都对这一结论如此乐观。

paras.en: The ability to identify such structures could offer a powerful molecular window into the physiology of long-extinct animals, including their metabolism and even activity levels, says paleontologist Kliti Grice of Curtin University in Bentley, Australia.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚本特利科廷大学的古生物学家克里蒂·格赖斯（Kliti Grice）表示，识别这种结构的能力可以为了解早已灭绝的动物的生理学提供一个强大的分子窗口，包括它们的新陈代谢甚至活动水平。

paras.en: The bone, from a fossil-rich site in northeastern Brazil called Mina Pedra Branca, belonged to the dinosaur Aratasaurus museunacionali. Grice and her colleagues used a variety of chemical and imaging analyses to study the Cretaceous Period specimen.
paras.zh: 这块骨头来自巴西东北部一个富含化石的地点，名为白礁岛，属于恐龙阿拉塔龙。格赖斯和她的同事使用各种化学和成像分析来研究白垩纪时期的标本。

paras.en: The team prepared thin cross-sectional slices of bone and imaged details of the limb bone’s internal structure with focused electron beams. That revealed ellipse-shaped microstructures within the limb’s fossilized network of blood vessels.
paras.zh: 研究小组准备了薄薄的骨骼横截面切片，并用聚焦电子束对四肢骨的内部结构细节进行了成像。这揭示了肢体化石血管网络内的椭圆形微观结构。

paras.en: A map of the ellipsoids’ chemical element composition revealed that they were full of iron, carbon and nitrogen, all components of a biomolecule called heme. Heme is an iron-bearing, ring-shaped molecule found in hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen throughout the body.
paras.zh: 这些椭球体的化学元素组成图显示，它们富含铁、碳和氮，这些都是称为血红素的生物分子的成分。血红素是血红蛋白中发现的一种含铁环形分子，血红蛋白是红细胞中的蛋白质，可将氧气输送到全身。

paras.en: Then, the researchers used a technique that identifies molecules by how they scatter laser light. Those analyses suggested the presence of porphyrins, ringlike organic compounds found in blood — and the precursors of heme. Finally, they ruled out contamination from other porphyrins, such as the pigment chlorophyll, by separating and identifying the molecular contents of a bone extract. That experiment also suggested heme.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员使用了一种通过分子散射激光的方式来识别分子的技术。这些分析表明血液中存在卟啉、环状有机化合物以及血红素的前体。最后，他们通过分离和鉴定骨提取物的分子含量，排除了其他卟啉（例如色素叶绿素）的污染。该实验还表明了血红素。

paras.en: Taken together, these findings point unequivocally to the preservation of molecular traces of ancient blood, the team says. They also offer a clue to a novel pathway that might preserve those traces for so many millions of years.
paras.zh: 研究小组表示，总的来说，这些发现明确表明古代血液的分子痕迹得到了保存。它们还提供了一条新途径的线索，该途径可能会将这些痕迹保存数百万年。

paras.en: Blood cells decompose within days of the death of an organism. Only unusual and fast-acting environmental and biochemical conditions could have stopped decay and held those tissues in place as the organism fossilizes.
paras.zh: 生物体死亡后几天内血细胞就会分解。只有不寻常且快速作用的环境和生化条件才能阻止腐烂，并在生物体石化时将这些组织固定在适当的位置。

paras.en: In this fossil, the secret ingredient was a manganese oxide mineral called hausmannite, the researchers say. The team’s analyses had found the mineral within the ellipsoid structures. That mineral, they propose, may have acted as a time capsule, preserving the cellular structures and protecting the molecules within, including collagen amino acids.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，在这块化石中，秘密成分是一种称为黑锰矿的氧化锰矿物。该团队的分析发现了椭球体结构中的矿物。他们提出，这种矿物质可能起到了时间胶囊的作用，保存了细胞结构并保护了其中的分子，包括胶原蛋白氨基酸。

paras.en: Distinguishing fossilized blood cells from nonorganic minerals that formed within a fossil after the organism’s death is a tricky task. During fossilization, mineral-rich fluids seep in and around the bones, and the minerals that form within the fossil can bear a strong resemblance to bodily structures.
paras.zh: 将化石血细胞与有机体死亡后化石中形成的无机矿物质区分开来是一项艰巨的任务。在石化过程中，富含矿物质的液体渗入骨骼内部和周围，化石内形成的矿物质与身体结构非常相似。

paras.en: In a 1997 study, two paleontologists analyzed tiny spheres found inside the limb of a fossil, possibly a pterosaur. The spheres were once thought to be the fossilized remnants of ancient blood cells, but the duo determined that the spheres were instead pyrite, an iron mineral that had been deposited in the bones after death.
paras.zh: In a 1997 study, two paleontologists analyzed tiny spheres found inside the limb of a fossil, possibly a pterosaur.这些球体曾经被认为是古代血细胞的化石残留物，但两人确定这些球体实际上是黄铁矿，一种死后沉积在骨头中的铁矿物。

paras.en: Those paleontologists suggested that, going forward, several criteria should be met before proposing a blood cell origin for fossilized structures, including comparing the shape of the structures with that of living related organisms and identifying certain biomarkers in the structures. One of those biomarkers is heme compounds.
paras.zh: 这些古生物学家建议，展望未来，在提出化石结构的血细胞起源之前，应该满足几个标准，包括将结构的形状与活的相关生物体的形状进行比较，以及识别结构中的某些生物标记。这些生物标志物之一是血红素化合物。

paras.en: Grice and her colleagues say that their study meets these criteria. Unlike the pyrite, hausmannite was crucial to preservation, “rather than simply a mineral that replaced biological material after it had disappeared,” she says. The close spatial relationship between the hausmannite, the blood cell-like structures and the chemical signatures of heme “raises the possibility that mineralization helped stabilize, entomb and protect components of the original biological material during fossilization.”
paras.zh: 格莱斯和她的同事说他们的研究符合这些标准。与黄铁矿不同，黑锰石对于保存至关重要，“而不仅仅是一种在生物材料消失后取代它的矿物，”她说。黑锰矿、血细胞样结构和血红素化学特征之间的密切空间关系“提出了矿化在石化过程中帮助稳定、埋葬和保护原始生物材料成分的可能性。”

paras.en: But Mary Schweitzer, a paleontologist at North Carolina State University in Raleigh who was not involved in the new study, says she doesn’t think these findings do fully meet those criteria.
paras.zh: 但未参与这项新研究的北卡罗来纳州立大学罗利分校古生物学家玛丽·史怀哲 (Mary Schweitzer) 表示，她认为这些发现并不完全符合这些标准。

paras.en: The heme biomarkers, for example, don’t appear to be localized to the round structures alone, as would be expected in fossilized blood cells, but come from analysis of the entire bone. The proposed red blood cells also differ in size and shape compared with red blood cells from living birds and reptiles, she says.
paras.zh: 例如，血红素生物标志物似乎并不像在化石血细胞中所预期的那样仅局限于圆形结构，而是来自对整个骨骼的分析。她说，与活鸟类和爬行动物的红细胞相比，拟议的红细胞在大小和形状上也有所不同。

paras.en: Schweitzer is no stranger to skepticism over the discovery of ephemeral tissues in fossils. In 2005, she and her colleagues reported the first recovery of flexible, soft-tissue blood vessels from the 68-million-year-old fossilized leg bone of a Tyrannosaurus rex. It was a landmark study that sparked debate, including over how it would even be possible to preserve such tissues through deep time, as well as the most surefire way to detect them in the present.
paras.zh: 施韦策对化石中短暂组织的发现并不陌生。 2005年，她和她的同事首次从6800万年前的霸王龙腿骨化石中发现了灵活的软组织血管。这是一项具有里程碑意义的研究，引发了争论，包括如何在很长时间内保存这些组织，以及目前检测它们的最可靠的方法。

paras.en: “I am not convinced” that the research team has definitively identified heme compounds, Schweitzer says. “I do applaud them for bringing a plethora of methods to the study. Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence, and that does require state-of-the-art technology.”
paras.zh: 施韦策说，“我不相信”研究小组已经确定了血红素化合物。 “我确实赞赏他们为这项研究带来了多种方法。非凡的主张需要非凡的证据，而这确实需要最先进的技术。”

paras.en: No one really knows what a dinosaur’s red blood cell shape would be, let alone how the process of fossilization might distort the original shape of the structures, or allow heme-related molecules to escape their cellular confines over time, Grice says.
paras.zh: 格赖斯说，没有人真正知道恐龙的红细胞形状是什么，更不用说石化过程如何扭曲结构的原始形状，或者随着时间的推移让血红素相关分子逃离细胞的限制。

paras.en: And, she says, her team’s interpretation of the evidence doesn’t just rely on the observations of those structures. “[It] rests on the convergence of anatomy, morphology, mineralogy, elemental analysis and molecular chemistry,” she says. “That combination is critical.”
paras.zh: 而且，她说，她的团队对证据的解释不仅仅依赖于对这些结构的观察。 “[它]依赖于解剖学、形态学、矿物学、元素分析和分子化学的融合，”她说。 “这种组合至关重要。”

paras.en: As for whether other fossils might have molecular traces that have been preserved by hausmannite, “we simply don’t know yet,” Grice says. “But this type of preservation may not be quite as rare as we currently think.”
paras.zh: 至于其他化石是否可能具有黑锰矿所保存的分子痕迹，“我们还不知道，”格赖斯说。 “但这种类型的保存可能并不像我们目前想象的那么罕见。”

articles.title: Toxic secrets are hiding in Arctic ice
articles.author: Katherine Kornei

paras.en: Ice cores record Earth’s secrets, even the dirty ones.
paras.zh: 冰芯记录着地球的秘密，甚至是肮脏的秘密。

paras.en: Some of the cylindrical sections of ice extracted from the Arctic contain elevated levels of arsenic, lead and other heavy metals that circulated in our planet’s atmosphere in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Those pollutants, which have been tied to declines in IQ and higher rates of certain cancers, were probably emitted by a mining and smelting company in Montana whose grounds are now designated as multiple Superfund sites, the researchers report November 3 in Nature Sustainability.
paras.zh: 从北极提取的一些圆柱形冰块含有较高含量的砷、铅和其他重金属，这些重金属在 19 世纪末和 20 世纪初在地球大气层中循环。研究人员于 11 月 3 日在《自然可持续发展》杂志上报告称，这些污染物可能是蒙大拿州一家采矿和冶炼公司排放的，这些污染物与智商下降和某些癌症发病率较高有关，该公司的场地现已被指定为多个超级基金地点。

paras.en: The ice cores contain tiny particles that were once airborne — including pollutants, volcanic ash and salt from ocean spray — and fell to our planet’s surface within a few days or weeks. In polar regions, that fallout combines with snow and is preserved as ice.
paras.zh: 冰芯含有曾经在空气中传播的微小颗粒，包括污染物、火山灰和海洋喷雾中的盐分，并在几天或几周内落到地球表面。在极地地区，沉降物与雪结合并以冰的形式保存下来。

paras.en: Joseph McConnell, an environmental scientist at the Desert Research Institute, and his collaborators recently analyzed 10 ice cores collected across Canada, Greenland and Russia. The cores contained material that had fallen to Earth as early as 210 BCE, but the interval spanning the Industrial Revolution in the United States — from roughly 1870 to 1914 — was what caught the team’s collective eye.
paras.zh: 沙漠研究所的环境科学家约瑟夫·麦康奈尔 (Joseph McConnell) 和他的合作者最近分析了在加拿大、格陵兰岛和俄罗斯收集的 10 个冰芯。这些核心包含早在公元前 210 年就掉落到地球的物质，但美国工业革命期间（大约从 1870 年到 1914 年）引起了团队的集体关注。

paras.en: In the ice layers from that period, arsenic concentrations in some of the ice cores were up to 15 times higher than pre-Industrial Revolution levels. Because the heavy metal exposure has been tied to upticks in the rates of certain cancers, McConnell and his team set out to determine the most likely source of all that pollution.
paras.zh: 在那个时期的冰层中，一些冰芯中的砷浓度比工业革命前的水平高出 15 倍。由于重金属暴露与某些癌症发病率上升有关，麦康奈尔和他的团队着手确定所有这些污染最可能的来源。

paras.en: The largest increases in arsenic existed in the ice cores from Greenland. That finding was a big hint, McConnell says, because atmospheric circulation patterns tend to move material from west to east. “The only way you can explain that pattern of deposition is if the emissions are coming from North America,” McConnell says. “Had it been from Europe, we would have seen much larger increases in the Russian Arctic.”
paras.zh: 砷含量增加最多的是格陵兰岛的冰芯。麦康奈尔说，这一发现是一个重要的暗示，因为大气环流模式往往会将物质从西向东移动。 “可以解释这种沉积模式的唯一方法是排放是否来自北美，”麦康奈尔说。 “如果它来自欧洲，我们会看到俄罗斯北极地区的增幅要大得多。”

paras.en: The most likely source, the team concluded, was a massive copper mining and smelting operation in southwestern Montana operated by the Anaconda Copper Mining Company. It was one of the largest in North America during the Industrial Revolution and, unlike other copper mining operations in the area, it worked with copper ore that contained heavy metals like arsenic and lead. It was no secret that those toxic metals were entering the atmosphere, says Fred Quivik, a historian and the author of Smoke and Tailings, a book about the environmental history of copper smelting in Montana. “Ranchers and farmers started seeing their livestock die from arsenic poisoning.”
paras.zh: 研究小组得出结论，最有可能的来源是蒙大拿州西南部由阿纳康达铜矿公司运营的大型铜矿开采和冶炼厂。它是工业革命期间北美最大的铜矿开采企业之一，与该地区其他铜矿开采作业不同，它开采的铜矿石含有砷和铅等重金属。历史学家、《烟雾与尾矿》一书的作者 Fred Quivik 说，这些有毒金属正在进入大气层，这已经不是什么秘密了，该书是一本关于蒙大拿州铜冶炼环境历史的书。 “牧场主和农民开始看到他们的牲畜死于砷中毒。”

paras.en: Based on the concentrations of arsenic in the ice cores and models of how material disperses in the atmosphere, McConnell and his colleagues estimated that the Anaconda Copper Mining Company was emitting roughly 30 tons of arsenic per day into the atmosphere in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. By comparison, Chile, currently the world’s largest producer of copper and home to more than 20 mining operations, collectively emits roughly one quarter as much arsenic today.
paras.zh: 根据冰芯中砷的浓度以及物质在大气中扩散的模型，麦康奈尔和他的同事估计，Anaconda 铜矿公司在 19 世纪末和 20 世纪初每天向大气中排放大约 30 吨砷。相比之下，目前世界上最大的铜生产国、拥有 20 多个采矿作业的智利，其砷排放量仅为目前的四分之一左右。

paras.en: Beginning in 1919, the Anaconda Copper Mining Company installed devices near its smokestacks and other facilities to capture arsenic and prevent its release into the atmosphere. Arsenic emissions dropped by about 60 percent as a result, the ice core data showed, but by then hundreds of thousands of nearby residents had already been exposed for decades. That exposure could have been lessened, McConnell says, if the Anaconda Copper Mining Company hadn’t waited so long to install the pollution-abatement technology. “They delayed installation for about a decade.”
paras.zh: 从 1919 年开始，Anaconda 铜矿公司在其烟囱和其他设施附近安装了装置，以捕获砷并防止其释放到大气中。冰芯数据显示，砷排放量因此下降了约 60%，但到那时附近数十万居民已经暴露在砷中数十年了。麦康奈尔说，如果阿纳康达铜矿公司没有等这么久才安装污染减排技术，这种暴露可能会减少。 “他们将安装推迟了大约十年。”

paras.en: These new findings should be combined with census records to trace the effects of this pollution on human health in the 19th and 20th centuries, McConnell and his team suggest. “We hope that epidemiologists will take this information and really investigate potential impacts on human populations.”
paras.zh: 麦康奈尔和他的团队建议，这些新发现应与人口普查记录相结合，以追踪这种污染对 19 世纪和 20 世纪人类健康的影响。 “我们希望流行病学家能够利用这些信息并真正调查对人类的潜在影响。”

articles.title: Science to restore speech is moving fast. Here’s what’s next
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: Scientists are racing to restore people’s ability to communicate. Powerful AI-based methods to decode speech signals and predict words, along with advances in technology, promise success.
paras.zh: 科学家们正在竞相恢复人们的沟通能力。强大的基于人工智能的方法来解码语音信号和预测单词，加上技术的进步，有望取得成功。

paras.en: This episode of The Deep End: Talk to Me takes listeners through the breadth of scientific efforts to restore words, emotions and even gestures to people who can’t move or talk.
paras.zh: 这一集《深渊：对我说话》将带领听众了解科学努力的广度，以帮助无法移动或说话的人恢复言语、情感甚至手势。

paras.en: We’ll hear from Casey Harrell, a man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis who can no longer talk. A user of today’s technology, Harrell has a unique perspective on what he’d like to see improved for the technology of tomorrow.
paras.zh: 我们将听到凯西·哈勒尔 (Casey Harrell) 的来信，他患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症，无法说话。作为当今技术的用户，哈雷尔对于他希望看到未来技术的改进有着独特的视角。

paras.en: And as season two wraps up, listeners will be left with a reminder of the power of a voice: a piece of comedy from Jules Rodriguez, performed with his voice clone in front of a live crowd.
paras.zh: 随着第二季的结束，听众将记住声音的力量：朱尔斯·罗德里格斯的一部喜剧，在现场观众面前用他的声音克隆表演。

paras.en: “Being backstage and then seeing him come out, like, roll out his wheelchair, and everybody goes nuts because they’re like, ‘What is going on here? This doesn’t make sense,’” says Jules’ wife, Maria Aleandra Fernandez. “And every time I was like, ‘This is life. This is love. This is passion. What else is there?’ I don’t know that there’s anything else more powerful than what this guy is doing here.”
paras.zh: “在后台，然后看到他出来，就像推出轮椅一样，每个人都疯了，因为他们会说，‘这里发生了什么事？这没有道理，’”朱尔斯的妻子玛丽亚·阿利安德拉·费尔南德斯 (Maria Aleandra Fernandez) 说道。 “每次我都会想，‘这就是生活。这就是爱。这就是激情。还有什么？’我不知道还有什么比这个家伙在这里所做的事情更强大的了。”

paras.en: Laura Sanders: OK, I want to ask who your favorite comedians are and why. Who makes you all laugh?
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：好的，我想问你最喜欢的喜剧演员是谁以及为什么。谁让大家笑了？

paras.en: Jules Rodriguez: Pete Holmes and Mike Birbiglia are some of my favorites.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯·罗德里格斯：皮特·霍尔姆斯和迈克·比尔比利亚是我的最爱。

paras.en: [Audio] He was just like, I’m a bear, et cetera.
paras.zh: [音频]他就像，我是一只熊，等等。

paras.en: [Audio] The best part of sleep is falling asleep. That’s the only part you’re there for.
paras.zh: [音频] 睡眠最好的部分就是入睡。这是你唯一要做的事情。

paras.en: Jules: Their styles are different, but I have always gravitated towards their authenticity.
paras.zh: Jules：他们的风格不同，但我一直偏向于他们的真实性。

paras.en: Sanders: There’s another comedian who is extra meaningful for Jules: Conan O’Brien.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：还有一位喜剧演员对朱尔斯来说特别有意义：柯南·奥布莱恩。

paras.en: [Audio] Today is a bit of a different sort of episode. I’ll be talking to Jules and Maria.
paras.zh: [音频] 今天的情节有点不同。我要和朱尔斯和玛丽亚说话。

paras.en: Sanders: After MA had reached out, Conan invited the couple onto his podcast, where they connected about comedy. Conan still checks in on Jules every so often.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：MA 联系后，柯南邀请这对夫妇加入他的播客，他们在那里谈论喜剧。柯南仍然时不时地来看望朱尔斯。

paras.en: [Audio] It’s incredible to me that in our conversations, you’re very frank about the pain that you go through, and how intense it is. But you’re also always so positive and funny and, frankly, you give me a lot of [beep]. Which I find to be, well I hate it, by the way, first of all. Oh, get over it, Conan.
paras.zh: [音频]令我难以置信的是，在我们的谈话中，你非常坦率地讲述了你所经历的痛苦，以及它有多么强烈。但你也总是那么积极、有趣，坦率地说，你给了我很多[嘟嘟]。我发现，顺便说一句，首先，我讨厌它。哦，克服它，柯南。

paras.en: Jules: Conan is very special to me. Watching and listening to him helped me disconnect from the harsh reality of my life. And when I got to meet him and chat with him, it meant the world to me.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：柯南对我来说很特别。观看和聆听他的讲话帮助我摆脱了生活中严酷的现实。当我见到他并与他聊天时，这对我来说意味着整个世界。

paras.en: Maria Aleandra Fernandez: Having the most normal conversation with Conan O’Brien is something I will never get over.
paras.zh: 玛丽亚·阿利安德拉·费尔南德斯：与柯南·奥布莱恩进行最正常的对话是我永远无法克服的事情。

paras.en: [Audio] So he has a bunch of banked phrases. He’s going to play a few of our favorites. OK. I’m fine. I’m perfectly [beep] fine. [laughter] Come on man, are we doing this or not? Oh my God, oh my God. I’m destroying this marriage.
paras.zh: [音频]所以他有一堆储存的短语。他将演奏一些我们最喜欢的曲目。好的。我很好。我很好[哔]很好。 [笑声]来吧伙计，我们到底要不要这样做？天啊，天啊。我正在毁掉这段婚姻。

paras.en: MA: He really is so genuine and like, not only willing to talk to us, but really looks forward to talking. Like, I love talking to you guys. I’m not just doing it to be a nice person, which feels, you know, feels wonderful.
paras.zh: MA：他真的很真诚，很喜欢，不仅愿意和我们交谈，而且真的很期待交谈。就像，我喜欢和你们聊天。我这样做不仅仅是为了成为一个好人，这感觉，你知道，感觉很棒。

paras.en: [Audio] You have my love, my respect and we’re thinking about you guys all the time.
paras.zh: [音频]你们拥有我的爱、我的尊重，我们一直在想着你们。

paras.en: Sanders: As you were talking earlier, it made me think about what it means to make somebody laugh and to entertain them, and like how actually very, very special that must be. Just kind of, at its heart, it’s, it is joy and humans connecting. And so, extra special.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：正如你之前所说，这让我思考让别人发笑并娱乐他们意味着什么，并且喜欢这实际上是非常非常特别的。从本质上讲，它是快乐和人类的联系。所以，格外特别。

paras.en: MA: That’s the other thing I’ve learned mainly through Jules, about humor and comedy. And who were we watching yesterday? The NPR interview with Dave Chappelle.
paras.zh: MA：这是我主要通过朱尔斯学到的另一件事，关于幽默和喜剧。昨天我们看谁了？美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 采访戴夫·查佩尔 (Dave Chappelle)。

paras.en: [Audio] Dave Chappelle says he is very clear about his role as a comedian.
paras.zh: [音频]戴夫·查普尔说他非常清楚自己作为喜剧演员的角色。

paras.en: MA: And Dave Chappelle said something that is so spot-on. He said that comedians are how people metabolize things.
paras.zh: MA：戴夫·查佩尔（Dave Chappelle）说了一些非常准确的话。他说喜剧演员就是人们代谢事物的方式。

paras.en: [Audio] We’re like the nation’s kidney. We help everyone metabolize not just facts, but feelings around facts, or ideas. And jokes are just a shorthand for all of that.
paras.zh: [音频]我们就像国家的肾脏。我们不仅帮助每个人代谢事实，还帮助每个人代谢事实或想法的感受。笑话只是所有这一切的简写。

paras.en: MA: And I’m also a nerd and I’ve been reading some Greek tragedies and studying about how, you know, that’s also like the artists that help people metabolize feelings and emotions. And when he said that, I was like, that’s exactly it. And that’s what Jules has done.
paras.zh: MA：我也是一个书呆子，我一直在读一些希腊悲剧，并研究如何，你知道，这也像艺术家一样帮助人们代谢感觉和情绪。当他这么说时，我想，就是这样。这就是朱尔斯所做的。

paras.en: It’s something that heals. And it’s not even like it’s self-deprecating. It’s not like, oh, let’s make fun. And the way he does it is so smart and genuine, but also not taking himself seriously. It just disarms everything. You’re just like, oh, OK. And that idea of metabolizing the really hard feelings that come around grief, mortality, losing a person, seeing how he’s trapped in his body, but he chooses not to be trapped in that really big way is so profound.
paras.zh: 这是一种可以治愈的东西。而且这甚至不像是自嘲。这不像是，哦，让我们开玩笑吧。他的做法是如此聪明和真诚，但也不把自己当回事。它只会解除一切武装。你就像，哦，好吧。代谢掉悲伤、死亡、失去一个人所带来的真正痛苦的感觉，看到他如何被困在自己的身体里，但他选择不被困在那个真正的大方式中，这种想法是如此深刻。

paras.en: Sanders: Science is iterative. It builds. It may take a wrong turn or two, but overall, it’s moving toward a deeper understanding of our world and of ourselves.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：科学是迭代的。它建立了。它可能会走一两个错误的弯路，但总的来说，它正在朝着对我们的世界和我们自己有更深入的了解的方向发展。

paras.en: By using their voices, by telling their stories, by telling their jokes, Jules and MA are helping me, and maybe you too, metabolize the pain – and the joy – of living. Welcome to The Deep End, Talk to Me.
paras.zh: 通过使用他们的声音，通过讲述他们的故事，通过讲他们的笑话，朱尔斯和马正在帮助我，也许你也是，代谢生活中的痛苦和快乐。欢迎来到深渊，跟我说话。

paras.en: [Voices] Hey mom, can I tell you something? Hi. Do you want to talk? That added layer of it being you. Hello? Your voice. Hi.
paras.zh: [声音] 嘿妈妈，我可以告诉你一件事吗？你好。你想说话吗？那增加的一层就是你。你好？你的声音。你好。

paras.en: Sanders: I’m Laura Sanders and today, we’re going to look ahead to what’s coming next for the human voice and efforts to restore it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我是劳拉·桑德斯，今天，我们将展望人类声音的下一步发展以及恢复它的努力。

paras.en: Sanders: In some ways, this podcast is a story of progress, of figuring out, little by little, more about the brain, and more about technology and more about people. Today, Jules can type with his eyes, and his son can hear his dad’s voice say I love you. In earlier episodes, you heard from Casey Harrell. Casey can think about saying a word to his daughter, and boom, they’re off playing a game together.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：从某些方面来说，这个播客是一个关于进步的故事，一个关于一点一点地弄清楚更多关于大脑、更多关于技术和更多关于人的故事。今天，朱尔斯可以用眼睛打字，他的儿子可以听到父亲的声音说我爱你。在之前的剧集中，您听到了凯西·哈勒尔的来信。凯西可以考虑对他的女儿说一句话，然后，他们就一起去玩游戏了。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: So this has kept me still in touch with people and the world, and it is not hyperbole to frame it this way.
paras.zh: 凯西·哈勒尔：所以这让我仍然与人们和世界保持联系，这样说并不夸张。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey has ALS and can no longer speak. He volunteered for a clinical trial, and now he has a device implanted in his brain that detects neural patterns as he tries to say a word. This system has changed his life.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症，无法说话。他自愿参加一项临床试验，现在他的大脑中植入了一个装置，可以在他试图说话时检测神经模式。这个系统改变了他的生活。

paras.en: Casey: It is the ability to parent my daughter. It is the ability to connect with my wife. It is the ability to make a wry joke with my friends. Timing is everything, and that is why having nothing, this is completely revolutionary.
paras.zh: 凯西：这是养育女儿的能力。这是与我妻子联系的能力。这是与朋友开玩笑的能力。时机就是一切，这就是为什么什么都没有，这是完全革命性的。

paras.en: Sanders: But there aren’t many people like Casey. Leigh Hochberg is the director of the BrainGate clinical trials consortium, the trial that Casey is participating in. I asked him how many people might have participated in similar sorts of research projects. How many people have electrodes in their brain that can help them speak?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是像凯西这样的人并不多。 Leigh Hochberg 是 BrainGate 临床试验联盟的主任，Casey 正在参与该试验。我问他可能有多少人参与过类似的研究项目。有多少人的大脑中有可以帮助他们说话的电极？

paras.en: Leigh Hochberg: In terms of actually decoding attempted speech, I’m almost sure it’s still less than 10. It may be closer to five or six, so far, and that number undoubtedly is going to increase fairly quickly.
paras.zh: Leigh Hochberg：就实际解码尝试的语音而言，我几乎可以肯定它仍然少于 10 个。到目前为止，它可能接近 5 个或 6 个，而且这个数字无疑会很快增加。

paras.en: Sanders: So this is a small but growing number. Growing, because we now have a solid scientific understanding of the brain’s speech signals, and other signals too. And neurotech companies are very interested.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以这是一个很小但不断增长的数字。不断增长，因为我们现在对大脑的语音信号和其他信号有了扎实的科学理解。神经科技公司对此非常感兴趣。

paras.en: Hochberg: About 10 years ago or so, the academic research had de-risked this field sufficiently that it allowed for the entry of now likely a dozen or more companies that are actively pursuing their own version of an implantable brain-computer interface.
paras.zh: Hochberg：大约十年前，学术研究已经充分降低了这一领域的风险，以至于现在可能有十几家或更多的公司进入该领域，这些公司正在积极开发自己的可植入脑机接口版本。

paras.en: What I anticipate will happen, what I guess I hope will happen, is that the companies will continue to very carefully, thoughtfully and in a very focused manner, create their systems, and test them rigorously. And hopefully they’ll be demonstrated to be safe and effective. And at the same time, the academic groups have the opportunity to continue to demonstrate what’s possible, to push beyond that, and to show hopefully what those medical devices, once they’re actually available to market, might be able to do next.
paras.zh: 我预计将会发生的事情，我想我希望将会发生的事情是，这些公司将继续非常仔细、深思熟虑、以非常专注的方式创建他们的系统，并严格测试它们。希望它们能被证明是安全有效的。与此同时，学术团体有机会继续展示可能性，超越这一点，并希望展示这些医疗设备一旦真正推向市场，下一步可能能够做什么。

paras.en: Sanders: I talked with Vikash Gilja, a neural engineer who works at a company called Paradromics. He sees this momentum that Hochberg describes too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我与 Vikash Gilja 进行了交谈，他是一名神经工程师，在一家名为 Paradromics 的公司工作。他也看到了霍赫伯格所描述的这种势头。

paras.en: Vikash Gilja: And, you know, we can see all the pieces coming together. These tools weren’t available even five years ago. And what we’re seeing is like, you know, month over month, there are new tools available. So we’re able to leverage those and move faster.
paras.zh: Vikash Gilja：而且，你知道，我们可以看到所有的部分都整合在一起。这些工具在五年前还没有出现。我们看到的是，你知道，每个月都有新的工具可用。因此，我们能够利用这些并更快地采取行动。

paras.en: Sanders: Paradromics has developed its own brain-computer interface for communication. The device is about the size of a dime, and it sits on the motor cortex. That’s the part of the brain that creates speech signals. The chip then detects these signals as a person thinks about saying a word.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：Paradromics 开发了自己的用于通信的脑机接口。该设备大约有一毛钱大小，位于运动皮层上。这是大脑中产生语音信号的部分。当一个人想要说一个词时，芯片就会检测到这些信号。

paras.en: Matthew Willsey: So the cortical module has 421 tiny little sensors.
paras.zh: Matthew Willsey：皮质模块有 421 个微小的传感器。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s neurosurgeon and biomedical engineer Matthew Willsey, of the University of Michigan Health. He’s describing the device from Paradromics here.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是密歇根大学健康分校的神经外科医生和生物医学工程师马修·威尔西。他在这里描述了 Paradromics 的设备。

paras.en: Willsey: They’re about one and a half millimeters long. And you know, it’s smaller than your thumbnail, like kind of all the way around. It’s like a cylinder. And at the bottom of the cylinder are the electrodes, is what we call them. And we get them really close to the brain. And then when we deploy it, what it does is it pushes those electrodes down into the brain.
paras.zh: 威尔西：它们大约一毫米半长。你知道，它比你的缩略图还要小，就像周围一样。它就像一个圆柱体。圆柱体的底部是电极，就是我们所说的电极。我们让它们非常接近大脑。然后当我们部署它时，它的作用是将这些电极向下推入大脑。

paras.en: Sanders: Those tiny sensors are listening to the nearby neurons that control the muscles required for speech.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些微小的传感器正在聆听附近控制言语所需肌肉的神经元的声音。

paras.en: Willsey: The principle is to try and get these things as small as possible to disrupt the least amount of tissue as possible, and then to get them really, really close to the individual cells, the neurons themselves that have the information we’re trying to record.
paras.zh: Willsey：原则是尝试让这些东西尽可能小，以尽可能少地破坏组织，然后让它们真正非常接近单个细胞，即拥有我们试图记录信息的神经元本身。

paras.en: Sanders: The goal here is to restore a person’s ability to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这里的目标是恢复一个人的说话能力。

paras.en: Willsey: So in the ideal situation, the electrodes would sit, you know, right next to those neurons. This type of technology that’s very intuitive, that can record activity from the brain in kind of a high-throughput way, can put the words up at a good speed and a good accuracy, allows them to kind of regain the ability to communicate with others close to how they maybe were before they had the illness. So that truly is very powerful.
paras.zh: 威尔西：所以在理想情况下，电极应该位于那些神经元旁边。这种非常直观的技术，可以以高通量的方式记录大脑的活动，可以以良好的速度和良好的准确性说出单词，使他们能够重新获得与他人沟通的能力，接近他们患病之前的状态。所以这确实是非常强大的。

paras.en: Sanders: You might remember that Casey’s implant, called the BrainGate 2 system, requires ports on his head that are connected to external wires.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：你可能还记得凯西的植入物，称为 BrainGate 2 系统，需要他头上的端口连接到外部电线。

paras.en: Casey: What is annoying about this device is really easy to answer. It is not portable, and it is not implanted only inside my head.
paras.zh: 凯西：这个设备令人烦恼的地方很容易回答。它不是便携式的，也不是只植入我的脑袋里。

paras.en: Sanders: Unlike Casey’s implant, the Paradromics device is fully implantable. That means it’s wireless. This summer, Willsey implanted Paradromic’s device in a volunteer’s brain. The brain belonged to a 68-year-old woman who lives in Michigan. She has primary lateral sclerosis, a disease that has taken away most of her ability to talk. So far, the Paradromics system is up and running, and the volunteer is testing her abilities out.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：与凯西的植入物不同，Paradromics 设备是完全可植入的。这意味着它是无线的。今年夏天，威尔西将 Paradromic 的设备植入一名志愿者的大脑中。大脑属于一位居住在密歇根州的 68 岁女性。她患有原发性侧索硬化症，这种疾病剥夺了她大部分说话的能力。到目前为止，Paradromics 系统已经启动并运行，志愿者正在测试她的能力。

paras.en: Here she is talking with Willsey and other researchers in a video provided by Paradromics. You’ll hear her natural voice, which is hard to understand, and then a digital voice speaking the words her brain implant decoded.
paras.zh: 在 Paradromics 提供的视频中，她正在与威尔西和其他研究人员交谈。你会听到她自然的声音，这很难理解，然后是一个数字声音，说出她的大脑植入解码的单词。

paras.en: [Audio] I love the change of seasons in Michigan. And my favorite one is the fall. I love the change of seasons in Michigan. And my favorite one is the fall. Yeah, it’s good.
paras.zh: [音频]我喜欢密歇根州的季节变化。我最喜欢的是秋天。我喜欢密歇根州的季节变化。我最喜欢的是秋天。是的，这很好。

paras.en: Sanders: This volunteer has used the device to talk to her grandkids on the phone. But this is just the very beginning for this research project. There’s so much more to test.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这位志愿者使用该设备与她的孙子们通电话。但这只是这个研究项目的开始。还有很多东西需要测试。

paras.en: Casey is still working on his system, too — particularly, streamlining the process. When Casey uses his brain-computer interface, it decodes speech signals from his brain, then puts words on a screen. Casey then selects a button, using his eye movements or his brain-computer interface, to say these words out loud with a digital voice. Here’s Casey.
paras.zh: 凯西仍在研究他的系统，特别是简化流程。当凯西使用他的脑机接口时，它会解码来自他大脑的语音信号，然后将文字显示在屏幕上。然后，凯西使用他的眼球运动或脑机接口选择一个按钮，用数字语音大声说出这些词。这是凯西。

paras.en: Casey: It is not fast enough to provide enough instant conversation with other people that need to slow down to talk to me.
paras.zh: 凯西：它的速度不够快，无法与其他需要放慢速度与我交谈的人提供足够的即时对话。

paras.en: Sanders: But scientists want to skip this middle part — the words written on a screen. They want instead to go straight to speech, and perhaps make conversations faster. Casey says this goal to go directly from brain signals to a speaking digital voice would be his top priority.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是科学家们想跳过中间部分——屏幕上写的文字。相反，他们希望直接开始讲话，也许可以让对话更快。凯西表示，将大脑信号直接转化为数字语音的目标将是他的首要任务。

paras.en: Casey: That one is the holy grail of what this will become in terms of speech. It will allow you to have a seamless conversation. I am talking about, yes, I will intend to talk, and then it will just translate that automatically into speech, like we do, and you are doing right now.
paras.zh: 凯西：这就是演讲方面的圣杯。它将使您能够进行无缝的对话。我说的是，是的，我打算说话，然后它会自动将其转化为言语，就像我们所做的那样，而你现在正在做的事情。

paras.en: Sanders: In an earlier episode, we talked about attempts to do just this with Casey’s system, to push it to do what they call brain-to-voice. Early attempts were hard to decipher. But it has already improved, by a lot. In the latest tests, this brain-to-voice process produces words that are understandable – reaching about 95 percent accuracy for listeners. Here’s Casey speaking test sentences. It comes from a preprint manuscript posted on the website bioRxiv.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在之前的一集中，我们谈到了尝试用凯西的系统来做到这一点，推动它做他们所谓的“大脑到声音”。早期的尝试很难破译。但它已经改善了很多。在最新的测试中，这种大脑到声音的过程产生了可以理解的单词——对于听众来说准确率达到了 95% 左右。这是凯西口语测试句子。它来自 bioRxiv 网站上发布的预印本手稿。

paras.en: [Audio] The day is not over yet. Please come in with me.
paras.zh: [音频] 这一天还没有结束。请跟我进来。

paras.en: Sanders: Scientists have another thing on their to-do list. And this one goes beyond the words themselves. Here’s Gilja, from Paradromics.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：科学家们的待办事项清单上还有另一件事。这超出了言语本身。这是来自 Paradromics 的 Gilja。

paras.en: Gilja: Let’s say I identify whether a sentence is a statement or a question. Well, now you can pass that information on to speech synthesis, so that you get these two different versions.
paras.zh: Gilja：假设我识别一个句子是陈述还是问题。好吧，现在您可以将该信息传递给语音合成，以便获得这两个不同的版本。

paras.en: Sanders: The same words could be a statement or a question. You see what he means. You see what he means? And that information can be pulled out from a person’s brain activity.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：同样的词可以是陈述，也可以是问题。你明白他的意思。你明白他的意思吗？这些信息可以从一个人的大脑活动中提取出来。

paras.en: Gilja: If I’m decoding prosodic information, if I’m decoding speed, when a word is meant to appear, that can also be passed on to modern speech synthesis systems, so that you’re more accurately capturing the prosody that somebody intends. Same thing with loudness, right? So you can see how as that information becomes available from the neural channels, it can be provided to the AI speech synthesis to get closer to the intended voice in the moment that the individual wants to generate.
paras.zh: Gilja：如果我正在解码韵律信息，如果我正在解码速度，当一个单词应该出现时，它也可以传递到现代语音合成系统，这样你就可以更准确地捕捉某人想要的韵律。响度也是一样，对吧？因此，您可以看到，当神经通道提供这些信息时，如何将其提供给人工智能语音合成，以更接近个人想要生成的时刻的预期声音。

paras.en: Sanders: All of these signals can be collected and used to build a more accurate voice — one that says things exactly how a person intends to say them, like a Minnesotan’s ooftah or a slow southern hey y’all. Now, today’s voice clones can add these emotional layers onto words already. Here’s what Jules told me when I asked him about whether his voice clone can do it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所有这些信号都可以被收集并用来构建更准确的声音——一种完全按照一个人想要说的方式说话的声音，就像明尼苏达州的“ooftah”或缓慢的南方“嘿，大家”。现在，今天的语音克隆已经可以将这些情感层添加到单词中。当我问朱尔斯他的声音克隆能否做到这一点时，这是朱尔斯告诉我的。

paras.en: Jules: Oh, there are plenty of things it does that are all the above. But one thing in particular is how it inserts tone and inflections on words. Sometimes my wife will get mad because my response can come off with some sass.
paras.zh: Jules：哦，它做了很多事情，就是上面提到的。但特别的一件事是它如何在单词中插入语气和变化。有时我的妻子会生气，因为我的回答可能有些无礼。

paras.en: Sanders: So there’s loudness, emphasis, pitch — all of these things contribute to what words means. But imagine if a brain implant can pick up these cues directly — no typing required. Here’s Hochberg.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以有响度、强调、音调——所有这些因素都有助于表达单词的含义。但想象一下，如果大脑植入物可以直接接收这些线索——无需打字。这是霍赫伯格。

paras.en: Hochberg: There’s a lot that can be conveyed through the emphasis, through the tone, through even the humor that can sometimes be conveyed by the way that somebody who’s able-bodied may speak a particular sentence. All of those, I think, really can be captured by these implantable brain-computer interfaces by harnessing the rich neural activity that’s available from the brain. We should be able to restore a lot of that.
paras.zh: 霍赫伯格：通过强调、语气、甚至幽默，可以传达很多东西，有时可以通过身体健全的人说某个特定句子的方式来传达。我认为，所有这些都可以通过利用大脑丰富的神经活动，通过这些植入式脑机接口来捕获。我们应该能够恢复很多。

paras.en: Sanders: Sergey Stavisky is one of the UC Davis researchers working with Casey and Hochberg. He and his colleagues are working on some of these ideas.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：谢尔盖·斯塔维斯基是加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员之一，与凯西和霍赫伯格一起工作。他和他的同事正在研究其中一些想法。

paras.en: Stavisky: And even now we’re continuing to improve that and actually adding additional layers. So we have one forward-looking project where we can maybe decode the kind of emotional valence of how he’s trying to say it. Is he trying to say something in an angry way or in a surprised way or in a happy-sounding way, to kind of further make it more expressive.
paras.zh: Stavisky：即使现在，我们仍在继续改进这一点，并实际上添加了额外的层。因此，我们有一个前瞻性的项目，我们也许可以解读他试图表达的情感价值。他是否试图以愤怒的方式、惊讶的方式或听起来快乐的方式说某事，以进一步使其更具表现力。

paras.en: Sanders: They’re even trying to decode singing. Well, OK, it’s really more of a hum at this point, he says. But those sorts of tone shifts could, in theory, be deciphered.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：他们甚至试图解码歌唱。好吧，好吧，现在更多的是嗡嗡声，他说。但从理论上讲，这些语气转变是可以被解读的。

paras.en: Stavisky: We definitely have our work cut out for us on the singing and melody side of things.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：在歌唱和旋律方面，我们确实有很多工作要做。

paras.en: Sanders: All sorts of voice signals could be pulled from brain activity.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：各种声音信号都可以从大脑活动中提取。

paras.en: Stavisky: Ultimately, we want people to be in full control of what they’re communicating. This should come from their intent. So, yeah, we are trying to decode all of the aspects of his voice, whether it’s the pitch, the timbre, the loudness, the intonation, which word he’s stressing. All of that, ideally, we would decode from brain activity, including kind of all of that emotional nuance.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：最终，我们希望人们能够完全控制他们所交流的内容。这应该是出于他们的意图。所以，是的，我们正在尝试解码他声音的所有方面，无论是音调、音色、响度、语调，还是他强调的单词。理想情况下，我们可以从大脑活动中解码所有这些，包括所有情感上的细微差别。

paras.en: Sanders: Voice clones can speak with various emotions. You heard my voice clone do just that in earlier episodes. But the difference here is that a person wouldn’t have to type in the instructions. They would come straight from their brain, seamlessly. Other nonverbal signals can be pulled from the brain, too.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音克隆可以表达各种情绪。你在之前的剧集中听到我的声音克隆就是这么做的。但这里的区别在于，人们不必输入说明。它们会直接来自他们的大脑，无缝地。其他非语言信号也可以从大脑中提取。

paras.en: Samantha Brosler: In the past five years or so, there have been a lot of advancements in the field of BCIs for restoring individual functions to people with paralysis.
paras.zh: Samantha Brosler：在过去五年左右的时间里，脑机接口领域在帮助瘫痪患者恢复个人功能方面取得了很多进展。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s Samantha Brosler, a bioengineer at the University of California, San Francisco. Some brain-computer interfaces can pick up movements. We haven’t talked much about them, but these implants have their own very successful research history. They’ve allowed people to control a robotic arm, for instance.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是萨曼莎·布罗斯勒，加州大学旧金山分校的生物工程师。一些脑机接口可以接收动作。我们没有过多谈论它们，但这些植入物有自己非常成功的研究历史。例如，他们允许人们控制机械臂。

paras.en: Brosler: Most of these devices so far have been designed to restore one function at a time, whereas in reality, frequently people who are paralyzed are missing both the ability to speak and perform body movements. And so in this study, we asked whether a single brain implant could be used to decode both speech and movement at the same time.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：到目前为止，大多数这些设备的设计目的都是一次恢复一种功能，而实际上，瘫痪的人经常丧失说话和进行身体运动的能力。因此，在这项研究中，我们询问是否可以使用单个大脑植入物同时解码语音和运动。

paras.en: Sanders: It turns out, it could. She and her colleagues were able to decode gestures for communication — things like thumbs up, or a head nodding yes — and words. This combo approach is a more natural way of getting a point across.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：事实证明，可以。她和她的同事能够解读交流手势（例如竖起大拇指或点头表示同意）和言语。这种组合方法是一种更自然的表达观点的方式。

paras.en: Brosler: We naturally use gestures alongside our speech. So for example, some gestures can substitute for speech entirely, like nodding yes, shaking your head no, waving, shrugging, giving a thumbs up. But they can also add or change the meaning of what we’re saying. So for example, if you say maybe combined with nod head yes, that has a very different, you know, meaning than if you say maybe and shrug or shake your head no.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们在讲话时自然会使用手势。例如，某些手势可以完全替代言语，例如点头“是”、摇头“不”、挥手、耸肩、竖起大拇指。但他们也可以添加或改变我们所说的话的含义。例如，如果你说“也许”加上点头“是”，这与你说“也许”然后耸耸肩或摇头“不”的含义非常不同。

paras.en: Sanders: My kids know that a slow maybe with a skeptical eyebrow raise is much closer to a no than my fast upbeat maybe with a little head nod. There is so much subtext in our body language.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我的孩子们知道，缓慢地扬起怀疑的眉毛可能比我快速乐观地点头可能更接近于“不”。我们的肢体语言中有很多潜台词。

paras.en: Brosler: So I think of, you know, gestures and body movements as an additional communication channel that can work together with speech to add expressivity to what we’re trying to say.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：所以我认为，手势和身体动作是一种额外的沟通渠道，可以与语音一起工作，为我们想说的话增添表现力。

paras.en: Sanders: In the study, the output was a digital avatar who looked like the person. Success looked like the avatar moving and getting the word right.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在这项研究中，输出的是一个看起来像这个人的数字化身。成功看起来就像化身移动并正确表达了意思。

paras.en: Brosler: And the idea is that we enable the participants to use speech and gestures alone or together. So in theory, someone could say hello while waving.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：我们的想法是让参与者能够单独或一起使用语音和手势。所以理论上，有人可以一边挥手一边打招呼。

paras.en: Sanders: The researchers started simple, with just a few phrases — hello, bye, good idea, how’s it going, let’s go — and just a few gestures, like a shrug or a point, a fist pump, thumbs up.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：研究人员从简单的开始，只有几句话——你好、再见、好主意、怎么样、走吧——还有几个手势，比如耸肩或点一下、握拳、竖起大拇指。

paras.en: Brosler: Of course, ultimately, we’re hoping to expand this to even larger vocabulary and more range of body movements across the whole body to help allow people more expression in their communication.
paras.zh: 布罗斯勒：当然，最终我们希望将其扩展到更大的词汇量和更多范围的全身身体动作，以帮助人们在交流中更多地表达。

paras.en: Sanders: The sheer number of different approaches to restoring communication is a sign that this neurotechnology is coming fast. Here’s Willsey.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：恢复沟通的不同方法的数量之多表明这种神经技术正在快速发展。这是威尔西。

paras.en: Willsey: I think it’s good. There’s a lot of players that are entering into the field that have a variety of different ideas where they can run the clinical trials and see how these different devices stack up.
paras.zh: 威尔西：我认为这很好。许多进入该领域的参与者都有各种不同的想法，他们可以进行临床试验，看看这些不同的设备如何叠加。

paras.en: Sanders: There are lots of reasons to be optimistic about the future here, and it’s a future that isn’t even that far off. Here’s David Brandman, one of the researchers at UC Davis who works with Casey. He’s also the neurosurgeon who implanted Casey’s device.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：有很多理由对这里的未来感到乐观，而且这个未来并不遥远。这是大卫·布兰德曼（David Brandman），他是加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员之一，与凯西一起工作。他也是植入凯西设备的神经外科医生。

paras.en: Brandman: I think I’m about five years away from being able to meet a patient with ALS and having the following conversation, and saying, you know, Ms. Smith, I’m sorry you’ve been diagnosed with ALS. I don’t have a cure for you, but I do have a device that I can implant that can help you communicate despite facing a future of paralysis. It’s a device that would be implanted. It’s fully wirelessly. It’s cosmetically invisible, and you’d be able to use it to communicate your needs and have a meaningful conversation with friends and family. So I think that kind of conversation is about five to 10 years away.
paras.zh: 布兰德曼：我想大约还有五年的时间我就能见到 ALS 患者并进行以下对话，然后说，史密斯女士，我很抱歉您被诊断出患有 ALS。我没有治愈你的方法，但我确实有一种可以植入的设备，可以帮助你在未来面临瘫痪的情况下进行交流。这是一个可以植入的设备。它是完全无线的。它在外观上是隐形的，您可以用它来传达您的需求并与朋友和家人进行有意义的对话。所以我认为这种对话大约需要五到十年的时间。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s a beautiful vision. When you’ve been a reporter as long as I have, you’re skeptical when scientists say something big is just five to 10 years away. But in this case, I see it.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是一个美好的愿景。如果你像我一样当了这么久的记者，当科学家说五到十年后就会出现重大事件时，你会持怀疑态度。但在这种情况下，我看到了。

paras.en: It’s easy to get drawn into the technical details here. Different types of implants, the decoding processes, AI-powered voice clones and what they can do and can’t do — what they should do and shouldn’t do. But if you step back and really look, you’ll see that this research is all propelled by a very simple and powerful fact: The human voice is too important to lose.
paras.zh: 这里很容易被技术细节所吸引。不同类型的植入物、解码过程、人工智能驱动的语音克隆以及它们能做什么和不能做什么——它们应该做什么和不应该做什么。但如果你退后一步仔细观察，你会发现这项研究都是由一个非常简单而有力的事实推动的：人的声音太重要了，不能失去。

paras.en: Casey: What does my voice mean to me? It means so much. I think it is the most important thing that I have lost in this whole disease.
paras.zh: 凯西：我的声音对我来说意味着什么？这意味着很多。我认为这是我在整个疾病中失去的最重要的东西。

paras.en: Sanders: So now we are here, in this moment, as Jules would say, right here, right now. And right now, the human voice is shifting and changing, expanding in ways that were completely unthinkable even just a few years ago. The future of the human voice and its many replicas is anybody’s guess.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以现在我们在这里，此时此刻，正如朱尔斯所说，就在这里，此时此刻。现在，人类的声音正在转变和变化，以几年前完全不可想象的方式扩展。人声及其众多复制品的未来谁也说不准。

paras.en: Sanders: In one of Jules’ comedy sets, the one he did in November of 2024, he wheels out onto the stage as the song “Walking on Sunshine” plays.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：在朱尔斯于 2024 年 11 月拍摄的一部喜剧中，他在歌曲《行走在阳光下》中推上舞台。

paras.en: As the crowd settles and finishes their clapping and woo-ing, Jules pauses. You can’t see this, but he wiggles his eyebrows — a lot. The crowd goes crazy every time. He hasn’t said a single word yet. After another pause, he deadpans with his voice clone: “That is all the time I have. My Make-A-Wish covered only a few minutes. Goodnight, everybody.”
paras.zh: 当人群安静下来并结束鼓掌和求爱时，朱尔斯停了下来。你看不到这一点，但他经常摇动眉毛。每次人群都会疯狂。他还没有说一个字。又停顿了一下，他面无表情地用他的声音克隆说：“这就是我所有的时间了。我的愿望只持续了几分钟。大家晚安。”

paras.en: And with that, Jules takes control and he’s off on a tear, ripping through stories of a weatherman who seems too happy about standing out in hurricanes, the exquisite guilt trips lovingly crafted by his Cuban parents, and the indignities of having body parts shaved with his sister right there in the room. Jules has the audience laughing so hard. It’s magnificent.
paras.zh: 就这样，朱尔斯掌控了一切，他泪流满面，讲述了一个天气预报员似乎太高兴在飓风中脱颖而出的故事，他的古巴父母精心设计的精致内疚之旅，以及和他的妹妹一起在房间里剃掉身体部位的侮辱。朱尔斯让观众笑得很厉害。太棒了。

paras.en: MA: And being backstage and then seeing him come out, like roll out in his wheelchair and everybody go nuts because they’re like, what is going on here? Like, this doesn’t make sense. And every time I was like, this is like life. This is love. This is passion. This is like, what else is there? Like, I don’t know that there’s anything else more powerful than what this guy is doing here and what I can help him do.
paras.zh: MA：在后台，然后看到他出来，就像坐在轮椅上一样，每个人都疯了，因为他们会想，这里发生了什么事？就像，这没有意义。每次我都想，这就像生活。这就是爱。这就是激情。这就像，还有什么？就像，我不知道还有什么比这个人在这里所做的事情以及我可以帮助他做的事情更强大的了。

paras.en: Sanders: I get what MA meant when she said that comedy is something that heals. When his set actually does come to a close, he tells the audience.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：我明白马的意思，她说喜剧是一种治愈的东西。当他的演出真正结束时，他告诉观众。

paras.en: [Audio] Now you have to watch me slowly get off this stage. Goodnight, everybody.
paras.zh: [音频]现在你必须看着我慢慢走下这个舞台。大家晚安。

paras.en: Sanders: It’s hilarious. It’s happy. It’s sad. It’s perfect.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这很搞笑。很高兴。很伤心。太完美了。

paras.en: This is The Deep End, Talk to Me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast, tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot. Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org.
paras.zh: 这是深渊，跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目的帮助很大。请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。

paras.en: The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Shute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund, with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: Power Grids on 5 Continents Pulse Every 60 Seconds. Scientists Think They Finally Know Why.
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: There are many things about modern life we take for granted – perhaps none more so than the vast electrical grids that power so much of it.
paras.zh: 现代生活中有很多事情我们认为是理所当然的——也许最重要的是为其提供大量电力的庞大电网。

paras.en: But for many years, these grids have been doing something strange.
paras.zh: 但多年来，这些网格一直在做一些奇怪的事情。

paras.en: Every 60 seconds, they pulse – a tiny change in the frequency that subsides only to recur 60 seconds later.
paras.zh: 每 60 秒，它们就会发出一次脉冲——频率的微小变化只会在 60 秒后减弱并再次出现。

paras.en: And it's not just one power grid. Around the world, multiple power grids – physically isolated from each other – have been found doing the same thing.
paras.zh: 而且它不仅仅是一个电网。在世界各地，多个电网（物理上彼此隔离）被发现在做同样的事情。

paras.en: It's precise, and it has persisted, year after year, for more than a decade. This precision suggests that it's not an accident, but it has remained a curiously enduring puzzle.
paras.zh: 它是精确的，并且年复一年地持续了十多年。这种精确性表明这并非偶然，但它仍然是一个令人好奇的持久谜题。

paras.en: Now, scientists think they have found the answer – and it's surprisingly mundane.
paras.zh: 现在，科学家们认为他们已经找到了答案——而且答案却出奇地平凡。

paras.en: Every minute, some uninterruptible power supplies – the backup systems used in places like hospitals, data centers, and research facilities – perform routine battery checks, creating small but measurable surges in electricity demand. And it's like clockwork.
paras.zh: 每分钟，一些不间断电源（医院、数据中心和研究设施等场所使用的备用系统）都会执行例行电池检查，从而造成电力需求小幅但可测量的激增。就像发条一样。

paras.en: "Even benign control routines can become systemically relevant when many devices act coherently," writes a team led by physicist Dirk Witthaut of the University of Cologne, Germany, in a paper published in Nature Energy.
paras.zh: 德国科隆大学物理学家 Dirk Witthaut 领导的团队在《自然·能源》杂志上发表的一篇论文中写道：“当许多设备一致行动时，即使是良性的控制程序也会变得系统相关。”

paras.en: "Unintended synchronization can generate recurrent and potentially amplified oscillatory behavior in large-scale cyber-physical energy systems."
paras.zh: “意外的同步可能会在大规模网络物理能源系统中产生反复出现且可能放大的振荡行为。”

paras.en: An electrical grid is always performing a delicate balancing act. At any given moment, the amount of electrical power being produced has to closely match the amount being consumed.
paras.zh: 电网总是在执行微妙的平衡行为。在任何给定时刻，产生的电量必须与消耗的电量紧密匹配。

paras.en: In Britain, there's a name for one of the most glorious examples of the challenge this presents: TV pickup.
paras.zh: 在英国，这种挑战最光荣的例子之一有一个名字：电视拾音。

paras.en: It describes the surge in power demand when large numbers of people collectively turn on their electric kettles to make a cup of tea during commercial breaks in TV programs.
paras.zh: 它描述了当电视节目插播广告时，大量人集体打开电热水壶泡一杯茶时，电力需求激增的情况。

paras.en: It's become less of a problem as grid operators have learned to anticipate it and streaming has gained popularity, but it can still generate massive demand during nationally popular programs such as royal what-have-yous and football matches.
paras.zh: 随着电网运营商已经学会预测这一问题，而且流媒体也越来越受欢迎，这已经不再是一个问题，但在皇家“有什么”和足球比赛等全国流行的节目中，它仍然可以产生大量需求。

paras.en: These fluctuations affect the frequency of the alternating current flowing through the grid – typically 50 or 60 hertz, depending on where in the world you live. When demand exceeds supply, the frequency dips; when supply exceeds demand, it rises.
paras.zh: 这些波动会影响流经电网的交流电的频率——通常为 50 或 60 赫兹，具体取决于您居住在世界的哪个地方。当需求超过供应时，频率就会下降；当供给超过需求时，它就会上升。

paras.en: Usually, these fluctuations are small and irregular, and grid operators work constantly to keep them under control.
paras.zh: 通常，这些波动很小且不规则，电网运营商会不断努力以控制它们。

paras.en: But a fluctuation that repeats with extraordinary precision every 60 seconds? Across electrical grids on five continents that aren't even connected to one another?
paras.zh: 但是每 60 秒就以非凡的精度重复一次的波动呢？横跨五大洲的电网，彼此之间甚至没有连接？

paras.en: Well, that's a whole new kettle of fish.
paras.zh: 好吧，那是一锅全新的鱼。

paras.en: Hints of the phenomenon date back to at least 2014, when researchers in Scandinavia documented unusual minute-scale fluctuations in grid frequency.
paras.zh: 这种现象的迹象至少可以追溯到 2014 年，当时斯堪的纳维亚半岛的研究人员记录了电网频率异常的微小波动。

paras.en: Such oscillations had been linked to hydropower systems, but similar patterns could also be found in electrical grids elsewhere – including continental Europe, Britain, Australia, and the United States.
paras.zh: 这种振荡与水力发电系统有关，但类似的模式也可以在其他地方的电网中发现，包括欧洲大陆、英国、澳大利亚和美国。
